_comment: Who holds a GUILD rank. Everyone else you fight shows a THREAT rank instead. Editor IDs are resolved by tools/EspGen against the vanilla masters (a typo fails the build) into adventurers.resolved.json. Order of checks: player -> already recruited -> current teammate (joins on the spot) -> joinOnRecruit exception (no guild rank until recruited) -> members -> chance groups -> none.
_members: Guild members from the start: anyone who can be a follower or hired. Custom followers usually add PotentialFollowerFaction; ones that don't are caught when they first become your teammate.
_named: Named NPCs the Guild has on its books whatever their factions say. npcs = editor IDs (resolved by tools/EspGen). level = the least level they have in game (raised in memory when the game loads, no record is edited), which also sets their rank: 24 is C. retiredWhen = a location, a keyword on it and the value that means they have taken another service (Sinmir is made captain of the guard when the Stormcloaks hold Whiterun: CWOwner 2); until then they are an active member. rank = the Guild rank they START at. One who has travelled with the player holds the higher of it and the rank of their level from then on, and never drops (Uthgerd, D, makes C at level 24); one who never has keeps it. note / retiredNote = a line for their SkyrimNet bio.

named.note: A seasoned C-rank adventurer who drinks at the Bannered Mare between jobs and still takes Guild Missives. Proud of his rank and sure he deserves a higher one; talks down to adventurers ranked below him, treats an equal as a rival, and is grudging toward anyone above. Holds the Whiterun guards in open contempt: an adventurer is paid when the job is done.
named.retiredNote: Was a C-rank adventurer until the Stormcloaks made him commander of the Whiterun guard; the Adventurers Guild set his name aside for it, and he insists that was the Guild's loss. Still judges people by their Guild rank, and runs the watch the way an adventurer would.

named.note: An adventurer who drinks at the Bannered Mare. The Companions turned her away after she killed a recruit in her trial, and she took her blade to the Adventurers Guild instead; she is proud of earning her rank on her own and bitter about Jorrvaskr. Hard, blunt and always ready for a brawl. Sinmir, who has always outranked her and says so, gets on her nerves.

An adventurer who roamed Tamriel for years before a Dwemer ruin cost her blade and nearly her life. She has not taken a missive in years and now gives herself to cleaning up Riften, but the Adventurers Guild keeps her name on its books and she is proud to be a member. Warm and encouraging to newer adventurers, level with her equals, glad to see anyone surpass her.

A scout of the Adventurers Guild who found the ore vein Darkwater Crossing was built on. She settled down when she married Verner, still carries her guild card, and misses the road more than she admits to him.

A sellsword and Guild adventurer who waits for patrons at the Retching Netch in Raven Rock. He calls himself the best swordsman in all Morrowind and takes Guild work when it pays. He grew up in Blacklight, spent years in Windhelm's Gray Quarter, and has had enough of Solstheim's ash.

A Nord beast hunter and smith of the Dawnguard who has carried an Adventurers Guild card for years and never gave it up. He hunted trolls and bears on Guild missives before Isran called him back, and still thinks of himself as an adventurer first.

_notes: Lines for an NPC's SkyrimNet bio that do not depend on their being a named member (above): someone who dreams of joining, the one who keeps a counter after an innkeeper's death, the one who has to say a town's counter has closed. whenDead = the line applies only once that NPC is dead. Editor IDs, resolved by tools/EspGen.

notes.note: Not an adventurer yet, though he talks of little else: a Rorikstead farmhand who dreams of registering with the Adventurers Guild, has practised signing his name for its ledger, and is in awe of anyone who carries a guild card. His father needs him on the farm and he has no armor.

Erik the Slayer, as he now calls himself: a farm boy turned adventurer, newly armored and eager to prove it. Guild ranks, guild cards and adventuring parties thrill him, and he registers with the Adventurers Guild the first chance the road gives him.

Since Hulda's death she keeps Whiterun's Adventurers Guild counter at the Bannered Mare. She talked her way into the licence because it is good business: adventurers are her best customers, and their trophies and reports are trade. She does the Guild's business only at the inn.
Since Hulda's death the Adventurers Guild's counter at the Bannered Mare is Ysolda's, not his, which he takes with a shrug. He sends Guild business her way.
Since Hulda's death the Adventurers Guild's counter at the Bannered Mare is kept by Ysolda; she points adventurers to her.

Since his father Corpulus died he keeps Solitude's Adventurers Guild counter at the Winking Skeever along with the inn, and takes the Guild's ledger more seriously than his father's jokes ever let him.
Since Elda's death he keeps Windhelm's Adventurers Guild counter at Candlehearth Hall: the cook who ended up with the ledger, and quietly proud of it.
Since Keerava's death he keeps Riften's Adventurers Guild counter at the Bee and Barb, as carefully as she did, and in her memory.

The Adventurers Guild's counter at the Silver-Blood Inn was Kleppr's, and it closed when he died: she has an inn to run and no time for a ledger. Markarth has no Guild counter now; she sends adventurers to another hold capital.
Her father Thoring kept Dawnstar's Adventurers Guild counter at the Windpeak Inn, and it closed when he died. Dawnstar has no Guild counter now; she sends adventurers to another hold capital.
Her husband Dagur kept Winterhold's Adventurers Guild counter at the Frozen Hearth, and it closed when he died. Winterhold has no Guild counter now; she sends adventurers to another hold capital.
Jonna kept Morthal's Adventurers Guild counter at the Moorside Inn, and it closed when she died. Morthal has no Guild counter now; he sends adventurers to another hold capital.
Valga kept Falkreath's Adventurers Guild counter at Dead Man's Drink, and it closed when she died. Falkreath has no Guild counter now; she sends adventurers to another hold capital.

_wanderers: Adventurers met on the road. They are Guild members with a rank from their level. npcPrefix: the game's own wandering adventurers, every NPC whose editor ID starts so (tools/EspGen lists them). names: any other mod's generic (not unique) person whose name has one of these words is one too (Immersive Encounters, Extended Encounters, Wyrmstooth ...), unless it also has one of notNames or they are in one of the 'not' factions. note: the line every wandering adventurer gets in their SkyrimNet bio. Mercenaries, sellswords and hired thugs are deliberately not here: Skyrim has those too.

wanderers.note: On the road between jobs, as a working adventurer of the Guild: takes Guild Missives from the hold boards, hands in reports and sells trophies at the inn counters, and carries a guild card. Talks shop readily with other adventurers (ranks, jobs, roads, what is paying) and measures them by rank: easy with an equal, respectful toward a higher rank, a little superior toward a lower one.

_joinOnRecruit: Followers whose story makes guild membership unlikely until they travel with you. They register when first recruited.

joinOnRecruit._npcs: Named NPCs treated the same way (Erik the Slayer is for hire, but only becomes an adventurer when the player takes him along; Frea of the Skaal and Talvas of Tel Mithryn would never sign up on their own). The Dawnguard's followers likewise: Celann was a Vigilant, Durak hunts vampires for his own reasons, Agmaer nearly signed as an E-rank before he heard of the Dawnguard, Ingjard handed her card back when she joined Isran, and Beleval was a bandit. Gunmar, who never stopped being a member, is under named.

_chance: Random world NPCs. The roll is a hash of the reference's FormID, so the same NPC always gets the same answer (no save data). kind: member = '(C)', retired = '(C, retired)', hidden = rank kept secret (only high Appraisal reveals it). First matching group wins.
